name: Fields of wheat and barley
method: grown and reaped from the earth by the nomads and few farmers of Urash before the boat folk came — their fields of wheats and barley; the land living simply and without much law

name: Fish of the two waters
method: offered in sacrifice to the deities of salt and fresh water at the first great temple

name: Barley bread
ingredients: barley flour; water; salt; date syrup or sesame oil for the fine loaves
method: barley ground in stone querns; kneaded and baked as flat loaves on hearth stones and in clay ovens; temple and palace workers issued bread as rations alongside beer
source_ref: Mesopotamian cuneiform record: Ur III temple and palace ration lists (bread issued to labourers); lexical lists naming many bread varieties

name: Barley beer
ingredients: malted barley; bappir (beer-bread); water; date syrup for sweetness
method: barley malted and part-baked into bappir loaves; fermented in great vats; drunk unfiltered through reed straws from communal jars; the brew sacred to Ninkasi goddess of brewing
source_ref: Sumerian Hymn to Ninkasi (Old Babylonian copies; brewing with bappir); Early Dynastic cylinder seals showing drinking through reed straws (archaeological record); beer and bread as the standard ration pair in Ur III lists

name: Dates of the south
method: eaten fresh and dried year-round; pressed for syrup as the land's sweetener; date-palm gardens shading the southern barley fields
source_ref: southern Mesopotamian agricultural and administrative record: date-palm gardens in cuneiform land and harvest texts; date wine attested in the cuneiform corpus

name: Dried river fish
ingredients: river fish of the Tigris and the Euphrates and their lagoons; salt
method: split and dried in the sun; salted and smoked for keeping; carried inland from the southern lagoons; issued to workers as rations
source_ref: cuneiform ration and offering lists (dried and salted fish as standard issues); fish bones in domestic middens of southern Mesopotamian sites (archaeological record)

name: Onions; garlic and leeks
method: planted in gardens and field edges; issued to workers as rations; the base of the pot — pounded into stews and broths; raw with bread
source_ref: cuneiform ration and garden texts (onions and garlic issued by the basket); attested crops of the Mesopotamian garden record

name: Lentils and chickpeas
method: boiled into thick pottages and stews with onion and leek; roasted; issued as rations with barley and oil
source_ref: cuneiform ration lists (legume issues alongside barley and oil); charred legume remains from Mesopotamian settlement sites (archaeological record)

name: Butter and cheese
ingredients: milk of cattle; sheep and goats; butter (clarified for keeping); cheese; sour milk
method: milk churned to butter and clarified for keeping; set and pressed into cheeses; sheep-run dairies supplying temple stores
source_ref: Ur III and Old Babylonian dairy administration (butter and cheese accounts of the temple sheep economy)

name: Sesame oil
method: seed pressed for oil; the ration-fat of the workers (the barley-beer-oil issue); burnt in lamps; used in cooking and unguents
source_ref: cuneiform administrative corpus (sesame oil issues and accounts; Akkadian šamaššammu — the ancestor of the word sesame)

name: Broths and stews
ingredients: mutton or goat; onion; leek; garlic; beer; barley; sesame oil; salt
method: boiled into broths and stews in the clay kitchen; seasoned and finished with oil; the cuisine recorded in the Old Babylonian recipe tablets
source_ref: Old Babylonian culinary recipe tablets (Yale Babylonian Collection; published by Jean Bottéro — broths and stews of the Old Babylonian kitchen)

name: Mutton of feast and offering
ingredients: sheep; goats; cattle for the great feasts
method: the temple herds supply the altars; after the offering the meat is shared at the god's table and among priests and guests; great feasts mark festivals and oaths
source_ref: Mesopotamian temple offering records (sacrificial sheep and goats; meat distributed to temple households); feast scenes in Mesopotamian art and texts

name: Grain — the base of the economy
method: the economy's price model anchors on grain — base 2 silver grains at reference stock 100; harvest inflow and drought stages move the price per the ratified constants (retunable; shown to the player as authored)
source_ref: DECISIONS.md D-011 (ratified INVENTED economy constants); docs/game-design.md §9.1; the drought it simulates: notes L15;L104

name: Drought fare
method: in drought stages the ration degrades — thin barley loaves; the beer ration cut; fish and dates stretched — flavor glue per the content policy (shown to the player as authored)
source_ref: DECISIONS.md D-011 (drought-stage price anchors); D-012 (content policy); docs/game-design.md §9.1; the drought that breaks the world: notes L15;L104; wb §4.1
